sentences.text: Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Civil Secrt. Lko.

And 3 Other Counsel for Applicant :- Shri Ram Maurya,Sagar Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant Smt. Rajrani, with a prayer to enlarge her on bail in Case Crime No.235 of 2022, under Sections 376, 302, 120-B, I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Bangarmau, District Unnao.
It is contended by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is mother of deceased and she herself lodged report on 06.06.2022 stating that her daughter was missing.

Thereafter, investigation was done and the statement of Munnu Lodh has been recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. in which he mentioned that co-accused Dhruv, father of the deceased had illicit relations with one Reena and she was abducted by him and she wanted to lodge report against Dhruv.
The statement further indicates that Dhruv co-accused wanted to save himself that is why he killed his daughter so that Reena could have been implicated in the case.

The report further indicates that co accused Hansraj,
Lalloo, Kamlesh, Ram Singh, independent eye witness have also given similar statement indicating the same fact.
It has been submitted that there is no any incriminating evidence found against the applicant and there is no justification to implicate the applicant, who is mother of the deceased.
Their statements do not show any corroborative evidence in committing the offence.
The evidence is very weak.
Learned counsel submits that the applicant is a lady and further requested for the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C.
The applicant has no criminal history.
The applicant is in jail since Smt. Rajrani vs The State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

Learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and contended that applicant was involved in plotting the incident and committing the crime as such the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

Without expressing any opinion on the merits, after hearing learned counsel for the parties and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, there is no direct involvement in commission of offence against the applicant, no incriminating evidence is found and case of the applicant is distinguishable from co-accused Dhruv therefore, I find it to be a fit case for bail.

Let the applicant, Smt. Rajrani be released on bail in the above case crime number on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.

It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The Trial Court shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led unaffected by anything in this order.
